takeaways.label: Record quarter, broad-based
takeaways.text: Highest-ever quarterly sales and profitability, with total income up 13.9% YoY and PAT up 24.6% YoY, driven by demand across domestic and export markets.

takeaways.label: Margins improved on cost discipline
takeaways.text: EBITDA margin reached 27.48% (up 136 bps YoY) as other expenses were held to 9.72% of sales through constant monitoring and better fixed-cost absorption, even with a slight raw material cost uptick.

takeaways.label: Phase 1 capacity is live, Phase 2 funded and on track
takeaways.text: Installed capacity rose to 54,000 MTPA; Phase 2 capex is underway with completion by September 2027 and a ~₹1,000 crore revenue contribution expected once it is in full capacity.

takeaways.label: Full-year 20% growth guidance reaffirmed
takeaways.text: Management is confident of maintaining or beating 20% revenue growth for FY27, with H2 seasonally stronger and first customer indications positive.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: The pace of Phase 1 capacity utilization ramp-up in Q3, progress on the two undisclosed new partnerships, and closure of the Privi Fine Sciences merger before fiscal year-end.

points.label: Revenue growth
points.text: Total income grew 13.9% YoY, supported by broad-based demand and the resilience of the business model.

points.label: Profitability leap
points.text: PAT grew 24.61% YoY, with EBITDA up 16.66% YoY; the conversion from EBITDA to PAT has improved significantly over the last 4–5 quarters due to better asset utilization and declining interest costs.

points.label: Margin walk
points.text: EBITDA margin improved to 27.48% from 26.12% prior year because other expenses were tightly controlled at 9.72% of sales through constant monitoring and optimum capacity utilization, spreading fixed costs over a larger base. Raw material cost as a percentage of sales was 52% vs 51% prior year, a slight increase attributed to CST/GTO sourcing variations across locations.

points.label: State incentives headwind
points.text: Only ₹1.62 crores received in H1 FY27 vs ₹9 crores in the prior year; excluding incentives, underlying EBITDA margins still improved due to expense control. Management expects more incentives in the next 6 months, with the FY27 total higher than the previous year.

points.label: Other income boost
points.text: Higher other income in Q1 and Q2 FY27 primarily came from foreign exchange gains, as the company is a net exporter and the dollar has been favorable.

points.label: Q2 seasonality
points.text: Q2 has been superior over the last 4–5 financial years because second calendar year contracts with some customers often bring newer products, resulting in better margins and profitability.

quotes.text: Babani: "We are confident of maintaining 20% or beating 20%, be honest. We are confident that we'll be able to be close to INR4,000 crores, maybe INR3,750 or some number, but we are close to guidance what we have given. 20% will be surely maintained."

points.label: Working capital cycle
points.text: Reduced to under 100 days from 124 days YoY; cash from operations reached ₹445 crores in H1, driven by higher profits. The long-term annual expectation is 105–110 days.

points.label: Receivables improvement
points.text: Receivables declined vs March while sales moved up because customers have been paying on time or even a few days early, reflecting Privi’s quality and delivery performance.

points.label: Return ratios
points.text: ROCE improved 216 bps YoY to 24.30%; ROE up 134 bps to 26.34%.

points.label: Leverage
points.text: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.07x; net debt-to-equity at 0.51x, indicating a strong balance sheet position.

quotes.text: Iyer: "Privi stands for quality on delivery time, and expectations of the customers have been so good with us that they have been helping us in ensuring that the money is paid to us on time and in some cases, maybe a few days before time also."

points.label: Phase 1 completed
points.text: Installed capacity increased from 48,000 MTPA to 54,000 MTPA as of 30 September 2026. Part of the expanded capacity volumes will come through in Q3 FY27, but significant impact is expected in Q4 FY27 when new annual contracts begin; utilization is expected at 85–90% for the expanded capacity in Q4.

points.label: Phase 2 timeline
points.text: Furfural-based derivatives (maltol, ethyl maltol, cyclopentanone, and specialty molecules) capex is underway with some expenses already incurred; completion expected between June and September 2027, with revenue contribution starting from October 2027. Full capacity of 12,000 metric tons is expected to contribute ~₹1,000 crores in revenue.

points.label: Phase 3
points.text: Capex of ₹400–425 crores, with additional revenue of ₹450–500 crores.

points.label: Combined 3-phase revenue
points.text: ~₹1,900 crores, fully in sync by 2030, enabling the company to reach the ₹5,000 crores mark under the 5K:1K plus vision.

points.label: New capacity offtake
points.text: During the 1-year project build, products will be manufactured on a pilot basis and sold to customers to sort out quality and other issues before commercial production starts; management described the customer response as positive, very positive.

quotes.text: Patil: "You will see part of it coming through in quarter 3, but a significant part would come in quarter 4 because that's when the new contracts really start, which are annual contracts. So we are very positive about those contracts. And you will see significant impact of that capacity utilization of almost 85% to 90% during that quarter for the expanded capacity also."

points.label: PRIGIV JV
points.text: Achieved its first profitable quarter in Q4 FY26 and continued profitability in Q2 FY27; Q2 FY27 sales of ~₹28 crores with positive PBT of ~₹2 crores; H1 FY27 sales of ~₹47 crores with negligible loss. Focus now on scaling and building a higher-value product portfolio. A process of converting debt into advances is in progress with large multinational companies. FY27–28 revenue guidance of ~₹225 crores, with a third phase being studied in pilot that could take it beyond that figure.

points.label: Privi Fine Sciences
points.text: Turnover of ~₹68 crores in FY26 with a loss of ~₹34.28 crores; capacity utilization at 85% but full capacity not yet realized due to pending regulatory approvals. Four out of five products are already being supplied to top multinationals. Regulatory approvals are nearing completion, with significant improvement in numbers expected next financial year; once permissions are in place, expansion will drive revenue from ~₹100 crores to the ₹250–300 crores mark. The merger process is expected to be completed before the end of the current financial year.

points.label: Raw material resilience
points.text: ~70% of revenue comes from non-petroleum source raw materials, so geopolitical tensions and freight volatility have limited impact on input costs. CST/GTO sourcing is very diversified.

points.label: End-market growth
points.text: Aroma chemicals usage is increasing significantly, with the Africa market growing and new applications and users of pinene emerging.

points.label: European headwinds as opportunity
points.text: Regulatory and cost pressures in Europe create opportunities for compliant, quality-conscious Indian manufacturers; Privi is positioned to capitalize on these shifts.

points.label: Next-year contracts
points.text: Management described the situation as extremely good with a very positive outlook for the market and customers, though declined to provide specifics, calling the details proprietary.

quotes.text: Babani: "See, our market's usage of aroma chemicals is increasing significantly. Lots of new things are coming, new people are using more and more pinene. Africa market is growing. So for us, we supply to markets -- customers who supply to Africa. So the markets are really growing well, and we hope to maintain the 20% target as committed."

items.title: ₹5,000 cr / ₹1,000 cr EBITDA target
items.text: Management targets ₹5,000 crore revenue and ₹1,000 crore+ EBITDA by FY29-30, more than double current levels, and reiterates 20% growth for FY27. The Givaudan JV is excluded from this guide, so JV ramp-up is upside on top of it.

items.title: Phase 1 debottlenecking completed
items.text: The ~₹300-350 crore Phase 1 expansion adding ~6,000 MTPA of existing flagship products was completed in Q2 FY27, with utilisation of the expanded capacity expected at 85-90% in Q4 FY27 as new annual contracts start. It carries ~₹450 crore of revenue potential, so volume benefit lands in earnings within two quarters.

items.title: Phase 2 new molecules (Maltol, Ethyl Maltol, Musk T)
items.text: The ~₹650-700 crore Phase 2 adding 12,000 MTPA of Maltol, Ethyl Maltol and Ethylene Brassylate is targeted for completion by June 2027, with trial production after and revenue from October 2027. At full capacity it carries ~₹1,000 crore revenue potential, and with over 95% of these molecules made only in China, existing customers are already sampling positively.

items.title: PRIGIV JV ramp with Givaudan
items.text: The 51:49 JV with Givaudan turned profitable in Q4 FY26 and reached ~₹28 crore quarterly sales with positive PBT in Q2 FY27, against ~₹130 crore expected for FY27. A ₹50 crore expansion is underway supporting ~₹225 crore revenue guidance for FY27/28, with a third phase under study that could take it beyond that.

items.title: Privi Fine Sciences merger
items.text: The merger of Privi Fine Sciences and Privi Biotechnologies into PSCL was approved by shareholders on 27 Oct 2026 with 89.72% of votes, and completion is expected before end-FY27. Fine Sciences brings 6,000 MTPA of installed capacity and ~₹300-350 crore revenue potential, scaling from ~₹68 crore FY26 turnover as utilisation and break-even arrive.

items.title: Phase 3 advanced speciality products
items.text: Phase 3, ~₹400-425 crore of capex for 12-15 advanced products including bio-route Cyclopentanone, is due for completion by September 2028 and adds ~₹450-500 crore of revenue. With overheads already covered by the larger base, management says every addition is accretive.

items.title: Furfural backward integration
items.text: In-house furfural manufacturing from corn cob, the next project after the current expansion, is targeted around FY28-29 in Gujarat using proprietary technology. It would make Privi the only player fully integrated from cob to Maltol, Ethyl Maltol and Cyclopentanone, in a vertical management sizes at ₹1,000 crore-plus of revenue.

items.title: Value-added specialty molecules
items.text: Four premium molecules (Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege, Privitolide) are being commissioned through FY27, with one already running, at the VAP plant that converts by-product streams into higher-than-portfolio-margin products. Customers have started awarding long-term contracts for these molecules, adding margin on raw materials the company already processes.
